summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of recurrent pulmonary emboli, chronic pain, COPD, and anticoagulation on Lovenox was admitted for worsening bilateral pleuritic chest pain and new right bicep pain. He was concerned about a new clot but showed no clinical signs of acute cardiopulmonary deterioration. A chest X-ray revealed no acute process, and a right upper extremity ultrasound showed no DVT. Pain was managed with a short-term increase in oxycodone from 5mg to 10mg every 4 hours, with plans to taper back to baseline. Anxiety was addressed with hydroxyzine and non-pharmacologic strategies. His condition stabilized, pain improved, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue Lovenox, taper oxycodone over 8 days, and follow up with pain management. No new clots were diagnosed during this admission.
problems: Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Diverticulitis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
